newsitem.title: CHINA: Taiwan-friendly U.S. senator arrives in China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan-friendly U.S. senator arrives in China.

text.p: Senior United States Senator Strom Thurmond, a staunch backer of China's political rival Taiwan, on Thursday arrived in Beijing on a visit that will include talks with Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian, officials said.

Thurmond, chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee and a fervent anti-communist, would spend four days in China at the invitation of Qiao Shi, head of the National People's Congress, or parliament, an NPC official said.

The Republican senator from South Carolina would meet Qiao on Friday and would fly to the seaside resort of Beidaihe on Sunday for talks with President Jiang Zemin and Defence Minister Chi Haotian, the official said.

Thurmond, who is president pro tempore of the Senate as well as one of the body's most long-standing members, would visit the northeastern city of Tianjin on Friday where he would watch a military demonstration, the official said.

Chinese and U.S. embassy officials declined to comment on the content of Thurmond's talks with Jiang and Chi, but the senator has strongly backed U.S. weapons sales to Taiwan, a policy Beijing vigorously opposes.

Communist Beijing has regarded Taiwan as a rebel province since the two were split at the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949 and opposes arms sales to the Nationalist-ruled island as infringing on Chinese sovereignty.
Taiwan has bought 150 F-16 fighter jets, batteries of Gulf War-tested Patriot anti-missile missiles and 1,299 shoulder-fired Stinger missiles from the United States despite Beijing's protests.
Taipei says a strong military is needed to defend against Beijing's standing threat to invade if the island abandons its pro-unification policy and declares independence.

Thurmond's visit is the latest in a long string of trips to China by U.S. lawmakers since late last year when Washington and Beijing began mending fences after ties were strained by disputes over issues such as human rights, trade and Taiwan.
